posts.cooked:
Hi @21f3000759 ,

In this question, please explain how can the last option(shown below) is also a correct answer.
I believe it’s not a correct option ; for example if the line contains multiple ~ITER~ this code will not work but the one given in the question and the other correct option will work perfectly irrespective of how many ~ITER~ are there in a given line.
This option (below) works only if there’s one occurrence of ~ITER~. Also, the code(below) by itself will not work because there’s no input to it(but I’ve assumed that the input is provided - btw, don’t do this in the exam and make us waste time unnecessarily on incorrect questions where we’ve to assume something and our assumption is wrong).

Please get back to me.

Thanks.

Regards

Rajagopalan Vaidyanathan

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
This option seems to be incorrect. @sayan could you please check Q13 option D (mock question)

Here is the working script -

c=0
while grep -q "~ITER~" testfile; do
  ((c++))
  sed -i "0,/~ITER~/s//${c}/" testfile
done

Note: testfile is the file having the data

Works for simple cases.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Yes this will not work as no input is provided to grep or sed, you can find updated PYQs here, this had been rectified there.
